title: Series and Parallel Circuits
learning_goal: Analyze, design, and construct series and parallel circuits and explain how current and voltage behave in each arrangement.

stages.title: 1. A complete circuit
stages.content: Electric current flows only when there is a closed conducting path and a source of potential difference. Circuit diagrams use standard symbols to represent batteries, resistors, switches, and other components.

stages.title: 2. Series circuits
stages.content: In a series circuit, components share one path. The same current passes through each component, and the source voltage is divided among the components.

stages.title: 3. Parallel circuits
stages.content: In a parallel circuit, components are connected across the same two points. Each branch has the same voltage, while current splits among the branches.

stages.title: 4. Worked comparison
stages.content: If one bulb is removed from a simple series circuit, the only path is broken and all bulbs go out. In a parallel circuit, other branches can still conduct current when one branch is opened.

stages.title: 5. Guided practice
stages.prompt: Three bulbs are connected in parallel to the same battery. One bulb burns out. What happens to the other two bulbs?
stages.hint: Each parallel branch has its own path to the battery.
stages.alternate_explanation: Removing one branch does not break the complete paths through the other branches.
stages.answer: The other two bulbs remain on.

stages.title: 6. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, read circuit diagrams, distinguish series from parallel connections, predict what happens when a component is removed, and explain current and voltage behavior in each type.
